name: copy_bytes_then_jump

name: print_text_via_dos_output
description: Opens a library through the system library table, measures a zero-terminated string from the caller's pointer and writes it out through the dos Output and Write calls.

name: scan_memory_region_types
description: Loops over 32 memory regions and, for each, tests up to 256 sample addresses through the exec TypeOfMem call. A region that reports a match adds 512 kilobytes to a running total and sets bits in two masks, one of which is set when a particular type flag is present; the totals are stored in shared variables.

name: open_read_and_validate_file
description: Opens a file through dos, seeks and reads it into memory allocated through exec, and checks a four-byte compression signature before returning. On any failure it writes an error through the dos Output and Write calls and then idles in a delay loop.

key: cannon fodder 2 (1994)(virgin)[cr pdx](disk 1 of 3)[h passwords crew - euroswap union]/Cannon Fodder 2 (1994)(Virgin)[cr PDX](Disk 1 of 3)[h Passwords Crew - Euroswap Union].adf:SSBOOT:0:05F6
name: decode_compressed_chunk
description: Checks a four-byte compression signature, reads the stored sizes and expands the packed data through a 384-byte stack buffer. It copies raw blocks and decodes variable-length codes into the output, calling four unnamed routines along the way.

key: cannon fodder 2 (1994)(virgin)[cr pdx](disk 1 of 3)[h passwords crew - euroswap union]/Cannon Fodder 2 (1994)(Virgin)[cr PDX](Disk 1 of 3)[h Passwords Crew - Euroswap Union].adf:SSBOOT:0:0714
name: match_table_entry_extract_bits
description: Scans a table of word pairs for the first entry whose masked value equals its stored companion, then reads a count and a shift from that entry. If the count is above one, it shifts a value, masks it with a stored word and sets the bit chosen by a computed index.

key: cannon fodder 2 (1994)(virgin)[cr pdx](disk 1 of 3)[h passwords crew - euroswap union]/Cannon Fodder 2 (1994)(Virgin)[cr PDX](Disk 1 of 3)[h Passwords Crew - Euroswap Union].adf:SSBOOT:0:074A
name: mask_and_conditional_call
description: ANDs two 16-bit values, then if one byte is less than another byte it calls an unnamed routine and returns that routine's result. Otherwise it returns the masked value.

name: return_empty_routine
description: The shown pseudo-code is only a return, so it changes no memory or registers. Two unnamed routines call it.

name: read_four_bytes_into_long
description: Reads four consecutive bytes from a pointer and builds them into one 32-bit value with the first byte in the highest position. One unnamed routine calls it.

key: cannon fodder 2 (1994)(virgin)[cr pdx](disk 1 of 3)[h passwords crew - euroswap union]/Cannon Fodder 2 (1994)(Virgin)[cr PDX](Disk 1 of 3)[h Passwords Crew - Euroswap Union].adf:SSBOOT:0:077A
name: build_canonical_code_table
description: Reads a count and fills a stack buffer of code lengths, then assigns bit-reversed canonical codes for each length and stores them with their masks in a table. It is the setup step for a variable-length decoder.

key: cannon fodder 2 (1994)(virgin)[cr pdx](disk 1 of 3)[h passwords crew - euroswap union]/Cannon Fodder 2 (1994)(Virgin)[cr PDX](Disk 1 of 3)[h Passwords Crew - Euroswap Union].adf:SSBOOT:0:08A8
name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: The routine decodes to bad instruction data after thirteen instructions and contains no usable behaviour. It is called by two unnamed routines, but its body is data, not code.

key: cannon fodder 2 (1994)(virgin)[cr pdx](disk 1 of 3)[h passwords crew - euroswap union]/Cannon Fodder 2 (1994)(Virgin)[cr PDX](Disk 1 of 3)[h Passwords Crew - Euroswap Union].adf:bootblock:0:023A
name: build_stepped_word_table
description: Fills twenty-eight four-word entries, counting a running value up by a step in the first half and back down in the second, with fixed words in the other slots. The facts list no hardware register, and the entry is called from the boot entry.

name: clear_memory_and_init_hardware
description: Clears nine pairs of words and a large block of memory, stores joystick and status port values in shared variables and writes fixed values to the interrupt, DMA, colour and copper control registers. It then waits on a shared flag, calls unnamed routines and re-enables interrupts and DMA from saved values.

name: build_display_copper_table
description: When a flag in its input is set, it fills a table of copper-style word pairs with wait and move values, then loops over eight rows of 32 words shifting bit fields into each entry. The facts list no hardware register, so the register targets are inferred from the values, and two unnamed routines are called.

name: call_two_unnamed_routines
description: Calls two unnamed routines in order and returns. The facts list one call, but the decompiled body shows two.

name: combine_nibbles_into_20bit_value
description: Combines the low nibble of the low word, the low word shifted right by four and the high word shifted left by eight, then masks the result to twenty bits.

name: return_empty_routine
description: The decompiled body is only a return, although the facts count 37 instructions. One unnamed routine calls it.

name: advance_timed_state_machine
description: Clears a block of table entries on its first call, then steps a small state machine. One state alternates between two table pointers after a fixed count, and another counts a stored value down to zero before resetting it. It calls three unnamed routines and returns the current state value.

name: return_without_action_entry
description: The decompiled body is only a return, though the facts count 28 instructions and one call that the body does not show. Two unnamed routines call it.

name: store_pointer_and_offset_pair
description: Stores the input longword as two words in one pointer pair, and the same longword plus a fixed offset as two words in a second pair. The facts list 123 instructions and two callers, but the decompiled body shows only the stores.

name: start_copper2_wait_raster
description: When a flag bit is set, it writes the second copper list address and the jump register, sets a shared flag by comparing a byte with a fixed character, and waits until a raster-position byte reaches a fixed value. It then calls unnamed routines and clears the flag; the facts also list the keyboard serial register.

name: spin_forever_when_flag_set
description: Enters an endless loop when a shared flag's fourth bit is set and otherwise returns without change. The write that follows the loop in the decompiled body is unreachable.

name: store_table_sum_deltas
description: Adds two table values chosen by offsets in a record and stores the sum back in the record, then fills 255 entries of a word table with differences between successive sums minus a fixed offset. The entry stride depends on a record flag, and two record offset bytes are advanced afterwards.

name: xor_bit_pattern_into_bitplane
description: For each of 44 rows, toggles one bit across eight bit positions in two byte locations, using offsets taken from table values and the record. It then advances four record offset bytes by fixed steps.

name: swap_and_store_screen_pointers
description: Swaps two longword pointers held in the record, computes a second pointer by adding a record offset and writes the low and high words of these pointers into shared globals, along with a pointer offset by a fixed amount.

name: configure_cia_timer_interrupt
description: Stores a handler routine address in a shared word and writes a fixed sequence of values to the CIA-B timer and control registers. It then enables interrupt bits through the interrupt enable register and clears a counter field in the record.

name: clear_flag_set_dma_interrupts
description: Clears one bit in a shared flag, then writes three fixed values to the device registers that the facts list as DMA and interrupt control.

name: scale_channel_levels_and_step
description: Calls one unnamed routine, then multiplies four table bytes by a current level and shifts each product down into spaced words of a record. It finally moves a level byte one unit toward its previous value.

name: store_scaled_step_difference
description: Computes a product of a shared value and a constant, divides it by the same shared value, and stores in the record the byte difference between two successive scaled counter values.

name: run_countdown_sequencer_step
description: Returns zero when a shared enable byte is clear. Otherwise it decrements a countdown in the record and, while it runs, dispatches four channels through a jump table; when the countdown expires it reloads it, clears four table entries, advances a wrapping index and points the record at the next table entry.

name: write_timer_and_request_registers
description: Writes a counter value, a derived value and a copied word to shared variables, then stores a fixed value with one bit set. The facts list the CIA-B timer, DMA and interrupt request registers, but the shown code writes shared variables only.

name: reset_audio_channel_registers
description: Adjusts a shared value, then writes eight table values into shared variables in sequence and finishes with a fixed value. The facts list the audio pointer and length registers for all four channels and the interrupt request register, but the shown code writes shared variables only.

name: undecoded_two_call_routine
description: The decompiler timed out, so only the instruction count, one caller and two unnamed calls are known. No behaviour beyond those facts can be stated.

name: find_table_entry_under_limit
description: Selects a nibble of the input byte according to a phase value stored in the record, then scans a table row of up to 36 words for the first entry that does not exceed a stored limit. It writes that entry to an output field and does nothing when the zero flag is set.

name: decrease_position_with_floor
description: Subtracts a delta from a position field in the record and raises the position to a fixed minimum when it falls below that floor. The result is copied into an output field.

name: step_position_toward_target
description: Calls two unnamed routines, optionally stores a step size from the input byte, then moves a position toward a target field by that step. When the remaining distance is smaller than the step, it snaps the position to the target.

name: add_delta_reset_to_reference
description: Adds a delta to a position field and, when the delta exceeds a second input value, replaces the position with a reference field from the record. The position is then copied to an output field.

name: store_and_offset_position
description: Stores the input byte in a record field when the zero flag is clear, then looks up a table value by a shifted index and scales it by a low nibble, negating it when a sign bit is set. It writes the position plus that offset to the output and advances a record field.

name: offset_position_by_table_value
description: Looks up a table value by an index taken from a record byte and scales it by the low nibble of that byte, negating it when the sign bit is set. It writes the position plus this offset to the output and adds a shifted amount of the stored byte into a second record field.

name: call_then_adjust_level
description: Calls one unnamed routine, then adjusts a level byte in the record from the input byte. A zero high nibble subtracts the low nibble and clamps at zero, while a nonzero high nibble adds it and clamps at a fixed ceiling.

name: adjust_level_by_nibble
description: Adjusts a byte level in the record using the input byte. A zero high nibble subtracts the low nibble and clamps the level at zero, while a nonzero high nibble adds it and clamps at a fixed ceiling.

name: store_byte_into_record_field
description: Stores the input byte into a fixed field of the record and returns.

name: set_index_scaled_clear_counter
description: Stores the input word multiplied by four into an index field of the record and resets a counter field to zero.

name: store_byte_and_call_routine
description: Stores its byte argument into a shared variable and then calls one unnamed routine. The branch for values above a threshold assigns the same byte again, so the stored value is unchanged.

name: advance_position_by_stored_step
description: Copies a nonzero input byte into a step field of the record when present. It then adds scaled multiples of that step byte to a 16-bit field and to a 32-bit field.

name: return_empty_routine
description: The decompiled body is only a return, so it has no effect.

name: stub_bad_raw_code_region
description: The facts count 5719 instructions in this raw region, but the pseudo-code shows only a bad-instruction halt. Nothing reliable can be said about its routines from this entry.

name: boot_block_io_raster_wait
description: Fills an I/O request with a fixed size and offset, runs the exec DoIO call, then loops with a delay and waits until a raster-position field reaches a fixed line. The shown code also writes a fixed colour value and triggers a trap, which the facts do not explain.

key: alien breed (1991)(team 17)(disk 1 of 2)[cr skr][t +10 legend]/Alien Breed (1991)(Team 17)(Disk 1 of 2)[cr SKR][t +10 Legend].adf:bootblock:0:009C
name: allocate_memory_then_issue_io
description: Restores a block of saved values, allocates memory through exec and waits until the result is nonzero, then sets up an I/O request and issues the exec DoIO call. It also writes the interrupt enable register before returning.

name: undecoded_copper_setup_routine
description: The decompiler timed out, so only the instruction count, three unnamed calls and a write to the first copper list pointer register are known. No behaviour beyond those facts can be stated.

name: call_single_unnamed_routine
description: Calls one unnamed routine and returns. Nothing else is done.

name: write_disk_length_then_call
description: Writes a fixed value to the register at a fixed offset from a base register, then calls one unnamed routine and returns. The facts list the CIA-A status register, which the shown code does not access.

name: fill_byte_set_bit_three
description: Writes all bits to a byte through an address register, then clears and sets bit 3, leaving the byte fully set. It returns its byte argument unchanged.

name: wait_while_status_then_clear
description: Clears bit 3 of a control byte, then calls one unnamed routine repeatedly while a status bit at a fixed offset stays set, and finally clears a shared variable. The facts list two calls, and the shown code makes one repeated call.

name: clear_shared_variable
description: Sets a shared variable to zero and returns. One unnamed routine calls it.

name: start_transfer_and_wait_status
description: Sets two control bits and writes the values 100 and 8 to two registers, then waits until a status byte at a fixed offset has bit 0 set before setting bit 0 again. It returns its byte argument unchanged.

name: busy_wait_delay_loop
description: Counts a fixed large value down to zero as a busy delay and then returns. Two unnamed routines call it.

name: scan_longword_bits_with_flag
description: Returns at once when a shared flag is set; otherwise it sets the flag, sets a bit in a record and loops over the bits of a longword, calling an unnamed routine after each full group of shifts. The branching on counter bits is visible in the shown body, but the body is cut short in the decompilation.

name: run_flagged_frame_update
description: Checks two shared flag bits: when the fifth bit is set it runs a few unnamed calls and sets a flag to a fixed value, and when the sixth bit is set it toggles a shared variable, makes a long sequence of unnamed calls and advances a counter that wraps at fifty. The facts list the interrupt request register, which the shown code does not write directly.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: Decodes to a short check followed by bad-instruction halts, so the body is data rather than usable code.

name: advance_random_state_value
description: Updates a pair of shared state values through a multiply, add and carry sequence, then returns the new state value. The shape suggests a pseudo-random step, but that is inferred from the arithmetic alone; one unnamed routine is called.

name: modulo_of_called_value
description: Adds one to a 16-bit input and, when the result is nonzero, calls one unnamed routine and returns its output value taken modulo that result. When the result is zero it returns the result itself.

name: patch_word_and_store_increment
description: ORs a fixed bit pattern into a word at an offset from an address register and subtracts a fixed constant from a longword that another register points to. It then stores its input plus one in a shared word, patching both locations in place.

name: step_nibble_table_toward_targets
description: When a mode value is one and a shared variable is zero, it advances a counter and, once the counter passes a limit, walks a table of 12-bit entries. For each nibble it compares the value with a target and adjusts it by a per-nibble step, counting the matches.

name: adjust_nibble_table_by_steps
description: When a mode value is two and a shared variable is zero, it advances a counter and, once the counter passes a limit, walks a table of 12-bit entries. It adds a shared per-nibble step to each nibble that differs from its target and then returns.

name: initialise_nibble_tables_for_mode
description: Sets a mode value to three, clears a block of 48 longwords and converts each word of a source table into three nibble values by dividing by fifteen. It stores the masked nibbles into a second table and resets a shared variable.

name: step_nibble_table_to_zero
description: When a mode value is three and a shared variable is zero, it advances a counter and, once the counter passes a limit, subtracts a per-nibble step from each nonzero nibble of a 12-bit table. It counts how many entries changed and branches on whether any did.

name: return_input_byte
description: Returns its byte argument unchanged and has no other effect. Two unnamed routines call it.

name: return_input_byte
description: Returns its byte argument unchanged and has no other effect. Four unnamed routines call it.

name: return_input_byte_entry
description: The decompiled body only returns its byte argument unchanged, although the facts count 25 instructions. Four unnamed routines reference it by address.

name: update_dma_on_flag_clear
description: When a shared flag is zero, it copies the flag to itself and, if bit three of it is set, writes two fixed values to the DMA and interrupt registers, then clears the flag. Otherwise it returns at once.

name: conditional_call_or_set_bit
description: When a state variable is nonzero but not one and a set of range checks hold, it either calls an unnamed routine at a counter threshold or returns its input with bit zero set. The range checks compare a shared value against four fixed limits.

name: conditional_call_or_pass_word
description: Applies the same gating as its neighbour: when the gate fires it calls an unnamed routine and returns that result, and otherwise it returns the input word unchanged. The range checks compare a shared value against four fixed limits.

name: update_value_on_change
description: Returns a value derived from its input or a shared pointer. When a shared variable is nonzero and differs from the last stored value plus a fixed offset, it stores the new value, calls an unnamed routine and clears a pointer slot.

name: clear_block_and_set_pointer
description: Clears a block of 129 longwords at a fixed address, sets a shared variable to a fixed value and stores a routine pointer in another shared variable when it differs. The facts list the interrupt enable register, which the shown code does not write directly.

name: update_audio_channel_three_buffer
description: When a shared flag bit is set, it chooses a sample buffer, writes the sample pointer, length and volume values for audio channel three, toggles a buffer selector and clears interrupt request bits. The shown code writes shared variables, while the facts list the audio channel three and interrupt registers.

name: copy_sample_block_to_buffer
description: Copies longwords from a source pointer into a fixed buffer in blocks of eight, with the count deciding how many blocks are copied. It sets a shared flag to a fixed value first, and the facts list audio channel three and the interrupt registers.

name: clear_shared_state_block
description: Sets twelve shared variables to zero and returns its byte argument unchanged. Seven unnamed routines call it.

name: clear_shared_state_block
description: Sets the same twelve shared variables to zero and returns its byte argument unchanged. Four unnamed routines call it.

name: clear_shared_state_block
description: Sets the same twelve shared variables to zero and returns its byte argument unchanged. Two unnamed routines call it.

name: clear_shared_state_block
description: Sets the same twelve shared variables to zero and returns its byte argument unchanged. The facts list ten unnamed calls and four callers, but the shown body only clears the variables.

name: start_queue_if_idle
description: If a shared pointer is zero, it stores its argument into two shared variables, clears another and sets a result flag to one; otherwise it clears the result flag. The facts list four unnamed calls, which the shown body does not make.

name: start_pending_queue_entry
description: Takes a pending value from a shared variable and, when it is nonzero, clears it and starts it if the shared pointer is zero, setting a result flag. Otherwise it clears the result flag. Five unnamed routines call it.

name: start_pending_queue_entry
description: Same logic as its neighbour: it takes a nonzero pending value, clears it and starts it when the shared pointer is zero, setting a result flag. One unnamed routine calls it.

description: Same logic as its neighbours: it takes a nonzero pending value, clears it and starts it when the shared pointer is zero, setting a result flag. One unnamed routine calls it.

description: Same logic as its neighbours: it takes a nonzero pending value, clears it and starts it when the shared pointer is zero, setting a result flag. One unnamed routine calls it.

name: start_pending_queue_entry
description: Same logic as its neighbours: it takes a nonzero pending value, clears it and starts it when the shared pointer is zero, setting a result flag. One unnamed routine calls it.

name: start_pending_queue_entry
description: Same logic as its neighbours: it takes a nonzero pending value, clears it and starts it when the shared pointer is zero, setting a result flag. The facts list two unnamed calls, which the shown body does not make; three unnamed routines call it.

name: advance_queue_entry_timer
description: When a shared pointer is zero it starts a pending value if one exists. Otherwise it counts a step and, when the count reaches the stored limit, runs an unnamed routine and advances to the next linked entry, clearing the queue when the link is zero.

name: gated_counter_and_call
description: Returns at once when a shared variable is nonzero. Otherwise it checks a stored state value against a few fixed values, resets a second counter in some ranges, calls an unnamed routine and advances that counter, which wraps at two.

name: advance_two_step_counter
description: Resets a second counter when a shared pointer is set and the counter is at least two, then calls an unnamed routine, advances the counter and wraps it at two. It returns its stack argument unchanged.
